# MATLAB energy and adaptive-damping repairs (#392, #409)

Base: v4 main `23aa3f0d`. Work is isolated from the v5 checkout. This ledger supplements the historical #305 and #315 qualification records; it does not rewrite their earlier results.

## Behavior and compatibility

- The standard `energy` factory evaluates only the coefficient families selected by the flow-component masks and present on the transform. QG does not fabricate wave coefficients. Existing energy units, names, masks and normalization are unchanged. Wave transforms retain the original elementwise wave-plus-vortex summation order.
- Adaptive damping keeps the original nondegenerate vanishing-filter expression. When a positive maximum equals the cutoff, the last retained mode has unit filter value and lower modes have zero filter value. This removes the unresolved `0/0` at effective maximum one.
- For the repaired allocated-`Nj>2` filter branch, effective vertical maximum zero has no resolved vertical variation. The vertically uniform mode has zero vertical damping; modes above the effective maximum retain the existing unit filter value. The C++ shared wave-forcing helper now uses the same zero-mode convention. The previous finite C++ `Qj(0)=1` would have imposed artificial damping through the finite `h_0(0)=Lz` deformation-radius normalization and was not adopted as a scientific oracle.
- The existing allocated one/two-mode fallback is unchanged; the reported defect and repaired degenerate vertical cases concern explicit filters whose effective maximum differs from a larger allocated transform.
- The horizontal filter itself is finite at maximum zero. A complete adaptive-damping operator still requires a positive resolved horizontal wavenumber: its velocity-dependent normalization uses `Delta=pi/k_max`. MATLAB now reports this unsupported setting explicitly, consistent with the existing C++ configuration rejection; no arbitrary finite viscosity is invented for this undefined full-rate case.
- The damping operator is rebuilt when either effective horizontal or vertical resolution changes. Cached resolution keys and derived output are published after construction succeeds. The new vertical cache is private and rebuildable, with no added persisted properties.
- Missing standard unqualified `energy` operations are restored before saved Eulerian field categorization, preserving any already registered user operation.
- MATLAB public signatures and annotated persistence schemas are unchanged. Existing files reconstruct the corrected diagnostics and filters through the existing factories.

## Focused regression scope

`TestEnergyDiagnostics` checks zero/nonzero QG states without changing their inactive wave placeholders, scalar `totalEnergy` agreement, registered/custom/empty component masks, exact unaffected wave summation, preservation of an existing user energy operation, and ordinary MATLAB Eulerian output followed by save/reload/continuation for all six transform families in both linear and nonlinear modes. Linear energy keeps its initial-only classification; nonlinear energy keeps its time series.

`TestAdaptiveDampingResolution` checks horizontal and vertical cutoff/maximum zero, one, and ordinary larger values; unchanged ordinary formulas; an explicit horizontal filter whose effective resolution differs from its allocation; unsupported unresolved horizontal construction; effective-vertical-only registry changes; and an undamped vertically uniform large-scale flow with nonzero velocity.

`TestPortableStableForcing.degenerateAdaptiveDampingMatchesMatlab` replaces the expected-MATLAB-NaN exception with direct RHS and ordered `SpatialForcingOperation` references, initial saved-output comparisons, and restored damping operators. It covers effective vertical maxima zero/one/two in all four wave transform families and both reference/native C++ providers. The maximum-one cases use an explicit 5-by-5 horizontal filter to exercise the collapsed horizontal interval too.

`TestPortableDiagnostics.allTransformDiagnosticsMatchMatlab` now evaluates the actual QG `energy` operation. Its complete existing six-family, odd/even, antialiasing, provider matrix replaces the historical `totalEnergy` workaround.

`TestWVForcingAndRK4` adds a hydrostatic/nonhydrostatic C++ regression proving that a large-scale, vertically uniform geostrophic state with effective vertical maximum zero acquires no adaptive tendency.

## Verification ledger

- Initial MATLAB numerical probe: script filename used a hyphen, so MATLAB `run` interpreted it as an expression and failed before project setup. Renaming the temporary script corrected the harness.
- Corrected numerical probe confirmed finite `h_0(0)=Lz`, exposed the artificial-damping consequence of the old C++ zero-mode convention, and reproduced stale vertical-only filter updates. No probe output was used as a passing regression.
- Focused C++ Release build and `forcing-and-rk4` passed, including the new zero-mode regression. The test was repeated after the helper's absolute-value normalization was moved before the new zero-maximum branch.
- First focused MATLAB batch: five methods passed (exact wave-energy regression and all four adaptive-resolution regressions); four methods failed. The QG test incorrectly asserted empty `Ap`/`Am` instead of the actual scalar-zero placeholders and inactive wave masks. Energy save/reload exposed missing restoration of the unqualified standard `energy` operation in `WVEulerianFields`, now repaired with the same missing-only guard used for component operations. Two numerical matrices stopped at native-provider setup because the isolated CMake build initially omitted the native FFTW flag. The pinned adapter was enabled before retry.
- First changed-file Code Analyzer: six MATLAB files, zero blocking findings. Transactional damping locals produced nonblocking property-name style findings; the local names were clarified before a focused analyzer retry.
- Corrected MATLAB retry: QG scalar/mask energy, user energy-operation preservation, both affected observer restoration tests, and both direct C++ parity matrices passed. The forcing matrix covers 24 family/resolution/provider cases and 336 ordered diagnostic channels, maximum relative error `5.217735914948311e-15`. The existing all-transform diagnostic matrix covers 48 configurations/provider cases and 2,232 variables, maximum relative error `1.2222953475043186e-13`.
- Energy continuation values and times passed on that retry, but its newly added nonlinear zero-forcing fixture emitted the pre-existing no-damping warning and failed the strict warning check. Adding an antialias-only closure retains zero RHS while avoiding that legitimate warning; the single-method retry then passed all six families in both dynamics modes (15.98 s). A test-loop indentation finding was corrected; its Code Analyzer rerun was clean. Production warning behavior was not changed.
- Final review covered the valid public custom-component case `WVFlowComponent(wvt,maskAp=1,maskAm=1,maskA0=selectedMask)` on QG. Because the transform's inactive wave coefficients are scalar-zero placeholders, family presence must come from its authoritative total-flow masks rather than `isempty(Ap)`. The helper now uses those masks. Standard saved-output verification above preceded this final presence-check revision; focused QG standard/custom-mask and exact wave-arithmetic tests verify the final revision without repeating the unrelated forcing matrix.
- Final family-presence tests passed (QG standard/custom-family selection: 1.39 s; exact wave arithmetic: 3.06 s). Code Analyzer was clean on the two changed files. Across the verification ledger, all 12 distinct focused methods passed and all seven changed MATLAB files have zero blocking analyzer findings. Final source hashes and numerical rows are recorded in `PortableRuntime/qualification/matlab-energy-adaptive-repairs-v1.json`.
- Combined-branch docs verification, required hosted CI, and integration: coordinator handoff; optional Full CI is not a development gate.
